item.title: India No. 1 Nagal apologises to local Portuguese crowd for post-match gesture
item.description: Sumit Nagal apologised to the Maia crowd and Portuguese player Henrique Rocha for making a “talking gesture” after his hard-fought first-round win at the Maia ATP Challenger. Nagal called it a heat-of-the-moment reaction and confirmed he had apologised personally to Rocha. The incident comes after India's disappointing Asian Games tennis campaign ended without a medal for the first time since 1986.

item.title: Silicon Valley’s “huge shortage”: Amodei calls Wang, Musk partners with a rival
item.description: Tech giants and startups face an unprecedented shortage of computing power, causing internal strife over resources, particularly within Google and its competitors. Collaborative efforts have sprung up, such as the partnership between Anthropic and Elon Musk's xAI, aiming to enhance computing capabilities. As the quest for computational resources intensifies, the rental costs of advanced technology, like the Nvidia H100 chips, have soared, prompting firms to explore alternative global suppliers.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Washington farmer challenges $618,000 irrigation penalties in state Supreme Court
item.description: Ron Fodé, a dedicated farmer from Washington State, is fighting against hefty penalties threatening his agricultural livelihood due to irrigation practices. The conflict arose in 2017 over water rights for his crops, leading to the Department of Ecology rejecting his irrigation assistance applications. This has resulted in penalties totaling $618,000.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: IPL has helped develop Kiwi players and coaches: NZC chief Geoff Allott
item.description: Ahead of India’s tour of New Zealand, NZC CEO Geoff Allott speaks to TOI about hosting the country’s biggest-ever series, record ticket sales, pitches, the IPL’s influence on Kiwi cricket and the enduring bond between the two nations.
item.dc:creator: NITIN NAIK

item.title: 'Mar gaya, mar gaya tera bhai': How row over metro seat turned deadly in Delhi
item.description: A tragic altercation on a Delhi Metro train claimed the life of Pawan Sharma, the sole breadwinner of his family, on October 8. His death has left his wife and two children in deep sorrow. Authorities have taken action, arresting the individuals involved in the confrontation over reserved seating, and the case is currently under investigation for culpable homicide.
item.dc:creator: ABHAY

item.title: 6.1-magnitude earthquake strikes off Panama
item.description: On Monday evening, Panama was shaken by a 6.1 magnitude earthquake, closely following a more powerful 7.7 quake that had already wreaked havoc. Homes, roads, and public infrastructure suffered severe damage, especially in Coclé province and Panama City. In response, the government declared a state of emergency to manage relief efforts, while the US Embassy alerted nations across Central and South America about possible aftershocks and tsunami risks.
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: Alex Trebek's $500K gift turned old rink into homeless shelter
item.description: In 2020, Alex Trebek and his wife, Jean, donated $500,000 to Hope of the Valley Rescue Mission. Two years later, their contribution had helped turn a shuttered, 60-year-old roller rink in Los Angeles into the 23,000-square-foot Trebek Center, a 107-bed homeless shelter designed to provide accommodation and mental health services to people experiencing homelessness.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: William Shatner sold his kidney stone for $75K to build a home
item.description: In 2006, Star Trek star William Shatner’s kidney stone fetched $75,000 at auction. Shatner said the proceeds, along with another $25,000 raised by the Boston Legal cast, helped Habitat for Humanity build a home in Louisiana for a family of five. The unusual auction turned a personal medical episode into a charitable contribution with a lasting impact.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Michael Dell, Intel co-founder Gordon Moore’s funds among 8 largest university gifts
item.description: In a groundbreaking philanthropic initiative, Ken Griffin has pledged $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, marking a historic moment in academia. This substantial gift will fund a new campus in Miami and enhance the School of Computer Science, while also benefitting strategic university programs in Pittsburgh. As the largest donation ever recorded in the realm of higher education, Griffin's generosity sets a new standard for philanthropic support in academia.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Man's restaurant chain employs hundreds of hearing-impaired, spreads joy
item.description: Ishara is a pioneering restaurant chain that champions inclusivity by hiring individuals with hearing disabilities to amplify the dining experience. Founded by Prashant Issar, the flagship restaurant was designed to prioritize exceptional service alongside high-quality cuisine. By utilizing straightforward communication techniques, staff connect effortlessly with patrons. Comprehensive training programs empower employees with vital skills, fostering confidence and a strong sense of belonging as they thrive at Ishara.
item.dc:creator: SMITA MISHRA

item.title: Oil prices hold near $105 per barrel as Trump eases sanctions on Russian fuel
item.description: Oil prices fell on Tuesday after increasing nearly $2 a barrel the previous session. Concerns over energy supply disruptions from ongoing conflicts in the Middle East influenced market sentiment. Meanwhile, US sanctions on Russian fuel were temporarily lifted, allowing for additional diesel supply. OPEC revised its demand growth forecast downward, indicating overcapacity in the market.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Naomi Osaka reveals how daughter Shai changed her life beyond tennis
item.description: Naomi Osaka has opened up about her mental health struggles, crediting motherhood and her daughter, Shai, with helping her find happiness beyond tennis. The four-time Grand Slam champion revealed how her perspective has changed since her 2021 French Open withdrawal, when she disclosed her battle with depression and anxiety. After defeating Maria Timofeeva at the China Open, Osaka reflected on personal growth, gratitude and learning to balance her professional career with life outside tennis.

item.title: 2036 Olympic hosts: Ahmedabad vs South Korea, Qatar, Munich, and 3 more
item.description: As Ahmedabad builds its case to host the 2036 Olympics, it faces competition from cities and countries with different advantages. From Munich’s existing venues and Qatar’s event-ready infrastructure to South Korea’s regional model, South Africa’s continental ambition, Istanbul’s Olympic experience and Hungary’s low-construction approach, each offers challenge, and lessons, for India.

item.title: Pope withdraws from Afghan league draft amid concerns over treatment of women
item.description: England batter Ollie Pope has withdrawn from the Afghanistan Premier League draft amid concerns over the Taliban’s treatment of women and girls. England cricket director Rob Key said participation was a personal moral decision, despite the ECB’s refusal to arrange bilateral series with Afghanistan. Former England batter Dawid Malan remains in the draft, highlighting the conflict between ethical concerns and players’ livelihoods.

item.title: Brain cancer diagnosis: Man blamed headaches on stress before scan revealed tumour
item.description: At first, Kash Raju dismissed his worsening health as the result of stress and a busy family routine. However, persistent headaches and dizziness led him to seek medical assistance, where a CT scan disclosed a diagnosis of grade 4 astrocytoma, an aggressive brain cancer. He promptly had emergency surgery and began NHS treatment, with a prognosis suggesting he may have only 12 to 18 months left.

This resulted in heightened security measures and barricades throughout Delhi, significantly impacting daily activities.
